claims.claim: USSF-385 is the fourth Starshield launch in 43 days from Vandenberg.
claims.episode_span: Four Starshield launches in 43 days from one pad show how quickly the Space Force is scaling its classified constellation.
claims.source_title: USSF-385 Caps 4 Starshield Launches in 43 Days, X Report 26 Sep 2026
claims.supporting_quote: SpaceX is preparing to launch USSF-385 from Vandenberg Space Force Base on Saturday, the third mission in a classified Starshield constellation buildout for the U.S. Space Force. The flight follows USSF-366 on Aug. 15 and USSF-153 on Sept. 10, each of which placed 23 satellites into orbit, plus USSF-259 on Sept. 17 with 17 satellites to a different orbital plane.

claims.claim: Cursor Security Reviewer reduced average review time from 4.8 to 3.8 minutes per session.
claims.episode_span: Average review time dropped from 4.8 minutes to 3.8 minutes per session, with developers accepting suggestions 60 to 70 percent of the time.
claims.source_title: Cursor’s AI bots now catch security flaws and halt bad deploys
claims.supporting_quote: Average review time has fallen from 4.8 minutes to 3.8 minutes per session, and developers are accepting the bot’s suggestions 60 to 70 percent of the time, up from 45 to 50 percent before.

claims.claim: xAI plans three waves of 220,000 GB300 GPUs to reach 1.44 million total chips.
claims.episode_span: xAI plans three waves of 220,000 GB300 GPUs each to reach 1.44 million total chips
claims.source_title: SpaceXAI Colossus GPU Expansion Nears 1.44 Million Chips, but Power Is the Real Test
claims.supporting_quote: Elon Musk says the SpaceXAI Colossus GPU expansion will add as many as 660,000 Nvidia GB300 chips before 2026 ends. If every planned wave becomes operational, SpaceXAI would have about 1.44 million AI accelerators across Colossus 1 and Colossus 2.
